slope_hard_deg.source: Lunar traverse planning guideline (traverses on slopes < 20 deg), Pena-Asensio et al. 2023, Acta Astronautica, doi:10.1016/j.actaastro.2023.10.010, as quoted in Universe Today / phys.org (Oct 2023)

slope_soft_deg.source: ASSUMPTION: start of the 'slow, careful' band below the 20 deg hard limit
slope_soft_deg.note: used for map coloring and for checking stop work areas

rough_hard_m.unit: m (std of detrended height, 8 m window)
rough_hard_m.source: ASSUMPTION: ~0.5 m of local relief within 8 m is treated as a blocky field a suited crew should avoid
rough_hard_m.note: DTM cannot see single rocks under ~1-2 m; Stack 'rocky' units add a cost

walk_speed_flat_kmh.source: Apollo 15 crew average walking speed rose from ~1 km/h (EVA 1) to ~2 km/h (EVA 2), Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, NASA (https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/static/history/alsj/a11/a11.gaits.html)
walk_speed_flat_kmh.note: lunar (1/6 g) experience; Mars is 0.38 g

walkback_speed_kmh.source: Apollo planners assumed 2.7 km/h for walkbacks longer than an hour (3.6 km/h for one hour), Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, NASA
walkback_speed_kmh.note: use the slower flat speed (2.0) for planning; 2.7 is the Apollo emergency figure

slope_speed_model.unit: speed(s) = v_flat * exp(-3.5*|s + 0.05|) / exp(-3.5*0.05), s = rise/run
slope_speed_model.source: Shape of Tobler's hiking function (Tobler 1993, NCGIA Technical Report 93-1), normalized to v_flat; ASSUMPTION that the Earth hiking shape applies to suited walking on Mars
slope_speed_model.note: Engine applies this per 2 m cell along the path direction

speed_factor_sand_large.source: ASSUMPTION: large bedforms (ripple ridges, soft crests) slow walking ~40%

suit_budget_min.source: xEMU designed for EVAs up to 8 h (6 +/- 2 h), NASA Lunar Surface EVA Concept of Operations (2020), https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/topic_1-_eva_lunar_surface_concept_of_operations.pdf

reserve_min.source: Legacy EMU: 8 h primary life support + 30 min backup life support (NASA EMU documentation; summarized on Wikipedia 'Extravehicular Mobility Unit')
reserve_min.note: kept untouched: the 'time home + reserve' alert fires before the reserve is needed

apollo_time_in_suit_min.source: Apollo planners treated a ~5 h time-in-suit limit as the main constraint on rover-assisted traverses, NTRS 19700009560 (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19700009560/downloads/19700009560.pdf)
apollo_time_in_suit_min.note: historical reference shown next to our 8 h budget

max_walkback_km.source: ~10 km max excursion a suited crew could walk back from after a rover failure (https://core.ac.uk/works/15254764)

work_min_science_stop.source: ASSUMPTION: observe, photograph, and sample one outcrop

work_min_depot.source: ASSUMPTION: ~4 min per tube for 10 tubes, loaded onto the rover

assumptions: slope_soft_deg: 15.0 deg - ASSUMPTION: start of the 'slow, careful' band below the 20 deg hard limit
rough_hard_m: 0.5 m (std of detrended height, 8 m window) - ASSUMPTION: ~0.5 m of local relief within 8 m is treated as a blocky field a suited crew should avoid

slope_speed_model: tobler speed(s) = v_flat * exp(-3.5*|s + 0.05|) / exp(-3.5*0.05), s = rise/run - Shape of Tobler's hiking function (Tobler 1993, NCGIA Technical Report 93-1), normalized to v_flat; ASSUMPTION that the Earth hiking shape applies to suited walking on Mars
speed_factor_sand_small: 0.85 x speed - ASSUMPTION: small bedforms (ripples) slow walking ~15%
speed_factor_sand_large: 0.6 x speed - ASSUMPTION: large bedforms (ripple ridges, soft crests) slow walking ~40%
speed_factor_rocky: 0.75 x speed - ASSUMPTION: blocky/talus units slow walking ~25%
work_min_science_stop: 45 min - ASSUMPTION: observe, photograph, and sample one outcrop
work_min_depot: 40 min - ASSUMPTION: ~4 min per tube for 10 tubes, loaded onto the rover
